title: Unauthorized access to student data at cloud provider
description: The cloud hosting provider's infrastructure could be compromised, allowing unauthorized parties to access full grade records, assignments, and account directory containing sensitive student information.
assumptions: Cloud provider has standard security controls but may have vulnerabilities or insider threats

title: Data used beyond original purpose by cloud provider
description: The cloud hosting provider could potentially use student data (grades, assignments, account info) for purposes beyond hosting, such as analytics, advertising, or selling to third parties.
assumptions: Cloud provider's terms of service may allow secondary data use; contractual safeguards may be insufficient

title: Direct identification of students through account directory
description: The account directory transmitted to the cloud provider contains personally identifiable information that directly identifies students, creating identifiability risks if data is exposed.
assumptions: Account directory includes names, IDs, or other direct identifiers

title: Linking of student identity to academic performance
description: Combining account directory with grade records and assignments at the cloud provider enables linking of student identities to their academic performance, creating comprehensive student profiles.
assumptions: Data elements can be correlated across the transmitted datasets

title: Potential violation of student privacy regulations
description: Transferring full student records to a third-party cloud provider may violate regulations like FERPA, GDPR, or other student privacy laws if proper safeguards and consent are not in place.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulations govern student data sharing with third parties
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction and institutional policies
